method: Presentation/network naming pass over cataclysm.exe. The exe keeps an alphabetical per-directory link order (Game/*.c then Win32/*.c), so each HW1 source file maps to a contiguous address window bounded by already-proposed neighbours; inside a window I aligned the binary functions with the ORIGINAL 2003 Relic source (GoK root ad1bb82, Game/ and Win32/) in source order and confirmed every pick by reading the Ghidra decompile against the source body: string literals, packet/command constants (e.g. 0xcccc COMMAND + COMMANDTYPE_n, 0xca00, 0xa1a1), struct sizes (CaptainGameInfo 0x2b0), globals shared with CET-named or already-verified functions, and caller/callee agreement with HW1 call sites (a confirmed function names its callees). The WON glue was named from TitanInterface's own debug strings ("TitanInterface::X ...", first string in decompile order = the method) plus the C wrappers that call each method. Front-end callbacks were named from the exe's {function, "FE_Name"} callback tables in .data matched to the HW1 tables. Inlined/merged HW1 functions are noted in the evidence; Cataclysm-only functions use the cat_ prefix. Only functions present in functions.csv are proposed (many FE callbacks are referenced only from data tables and have no Ghidra function yet). Front-end pass (resumed session): same window method applied to the FEMan-built screens and their glue - ConsMgr/LaunchMgr/ResearchGUI/TradeMgr managers, ShipView, PiePlate, Tactical, Tutor, GamePick/ScenPick/ColPick/FEReg leftovers and the mainrgn/SinglePlayer lockout and manager-launch callbacks - each pick confirmed against the ORIG (ad1bb82) body: kasf* sole callers for tut*/tm* wrappers, Save/LoadGame callers plus chunk sizes and the 0xb11db11d flag for save code, render-restart callers for texture load/free pairs, and literal strings; Cataclysm-only screens (dev console FEMan\console.fib, OverlayIcons) got cat_ names at medium.
